name: Persepolis — the terrace
scaleNote: 0.35 Studs pro Meter, Terrasse 6 m statt 14: bei 0,5 und 14 m waren es 97 338 Steine, und eine massive Terrasse waechst mit dem Kubus wie jeder Vollkoerper im Atlas.

terraceArea.source: Wikipedia, Persepolis: a '125,000 m2 (1,350,000 sq ft) terrace'.

gate.source: Wikipedia, Persepolis: the Gate of All Nations is 'a square of approximately 25 m (82 ft) in length, with four columns'.

throneHall.source: Wikipedia, Persepolis: the Throne Hall's '70 m2 x 70 m2'.

note:
THE TERRACE IS AN AREA, NOT A SHAPE. 125 000 m2 is the one figure the article gives for the platform, and an area does not say whether it is 350 m square or 500 x 250. This sheet builds 450 x 278 m, which is 125 100 m2 -- the right area in a rectangle nobody surveyed. That is arithmetic on a source dressed as a plan, and it is written here rather than left in `dimensions`.

NO APADANA DIMENSIONS AT ALL. The article gives neither the hall's size nor its column height nor its column count -- for the building Persepolis is best known for. The Gate of All Nations gets 25 m and 'four columns', which is why the gate is the one structure here built to a cited number in both its size and its count.

The Throne Hall's '70 m2 x 70 m2' is how the source writes it; read as a 70 m square, since 70 m2 x 70 m2 is not a dimension anyone could build.
